Title: Haiti gang raid leaves 47 dead, as residents demand stronger protections
Article:
PORT-AU-PRINCE: At least 47 people were killed and 22 more injured in an overnight gang raid on a neighbourhood overlooking Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, the UN said on Monday, prompting anger over the lack of protection from repeated deadly attacks.
The United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti said estimates could still change.
The hillside community of Kenscoff, in a strategic position overlooking routes into the capital, has suffered a dozen attacks by armed gangs since last year, forcing thousands to flee their homes.
Powerful gangs under a broad alliance have for years cemented their influence over Haiti's capital and expanded to nearby regions, despite attempts by foreign nations to reinforce the country's outgunned police.
Haitian rights group RNDDH estimated 30 to 40 people were killed and 15 to 20 wounded in the raid, which began around 10.30pm local time, but said it was difficult to assess a complete tally.
Even as Haiti's government decried a "heinous attack" and promised to reinforce security, residents demanded the local police chief step down, saying officers failed to protect people killed just minutes from the police station.
"Kenscoff will not be abandoned," the prime minister's office said on social media. "The government's authority will be restored, without weakness and without delay."
FORCED TO FLEE KENSCOFF
Attacks in Kenscoff over two months in early 2025 saw more than 260 people killed and 200 homes destroyed or set on fire, forcing 3,000 people to flee, according to UN estimates.
Nearly a dozen more attacks have taken place since, including rapes, kidnapping, arson and livestock theft.
[[nid:1518263]]
"My family are victims," said Coriolan Kendy, standing by his cousin's body, lying on the road in a blood-stained sheet. "People in Kenscoff are suffering and the government is to blame."
Another resident, Orisme, who did not share his last name, pleaded for the prime minister's support. "We live in humiliation and they do nothing for us," he said.
Some residents said several dozen police had tried to rebuff the armed men during the night, and some were injured. They added that they did not identify gang members among the dead.
Local media said several houses were set on fire, including the home of Jean William Pape, a leading public health expert.
"The police never gave up," national police chief Vladimir Paraison told reporters during a visit to Kenscoff later in the day.
Kenscoff overlooks routes into Petion-Ville — home to several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government — as well as a major road from the capital into southern Haiti.
The violence may deepen concerns over Haiti's ability to hold an election in December, its first in a decade. Successive governments have repeatedly postponed elections as armed gangs have expanded their influence.
The UN.-backed Gang Suppression Force, which is mandated to help police fight gangs, aims to reach a capacity of more than 5,500 troops this autumn.
A spokesperson did not immediately respond to questions on whether the troops were reinforcing Kenscoff security.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Children turn up in court to see man accused of setting mum on fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The children of the woman, 62, who was doused with petrol before she was set on fire, turned up at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court yesterday to catch a glimpse of the alleged assailant.
This happened even as the victim Gan Siew Teen's condition worsened. She is  warded in the Intensive Care Unit.
Gan's daughter, identified only as Yap, said her mother's condition had deteriorated even after undergoing four surgeries.
"Now she has bacterial infection and the doctors are arranging another surgery."
Yap was present in court yesterday with several relatives.
The family did not confront the man, identified as Ang Kam Tong, 59, an e-hailing driver, who claimed trial to a charge of attempted murder.
He  allegedly set Gan on fire at a lottery outlet in Kepong earlier this month.
Ang, who sat with his head bowed throughout the proceedings, maintained his innocence.
"Not guilty," he said from the dock.
He was was charged under Section 307(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a prison sentence of up to 20 years upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shakila Mohd Shariff appeared for the prosecution and urged the court to deny Ang bail, citing the severity of the victim's third-degree burns and a police report indicating that the accused had attempted to flee during his arrest.
However, lawyer Lee Keng Fatt, representing the accused, applied for bail.
"The accused is an e-hailing driver with no fixed income, is single and has siblings who may be able to stand as sureties," he said.
The court allowed the accused to be released on RM15,000 bail with one surety and fixed Sept 25 for mention and submission of documents.
It was reported that Gan was unlocking the premises when Ang approached her, splashed petrol over her body, ignited a lighter, and threw it at her before fleeing on foot. Gan, who lives within walking distance of her workplace, suffered burns on her face, neck, arms and body.
Following the incident Kepong  member of parliament Lim Lip Eng offered a RM5,000 reward to anyone with information on the incident.
Ang was arrested a week later in Kepong.

Title: Check how motor and home insurance policies work together, EV owners told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The recent fire at a house that started while an electric vehicle (EV) was charging has thrown the hidden costs of installing EV chargers and the insurance premiums that follow into the spotlight.
The discussion flared up online after the General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM) reminded homeowners to review their liability coverage to ensure they remained protected from such incidents.
PIAM chief executive officer Chua Kim Soon said standard houseowner policies typically capped public liability at RM50,000, although optional extensions were available to raise the limits.
He said homeowners should reassess their insurance policies to ensure the building's sum insured reflects updated rebuilding costs, including major home or electrical upgrades.
Chua said EV owners should also consider how their motor and home insurance policies worked together.
EV owners, especially those living in landed homes, reacted on social media, questioning how owning an EV could lead to higher insurance costs.
"And RM50,000 is too little to rebuild a house.
There is roofing, ceiling repairs, painting, electrical rewiring, plumbing, debris removal, and flooring.
Even a 1,200 sq ft property would need more than that amount," one owner said.
Another posted about how neighbours of EV owners now shared this anxiety following the Cheras fire.
[[nid:1518255]]
It was reported that installing a home EV charger would typically cost between RM3,000 and RM8,000 for a standard single-phase 7kW AC wall box, but this does not take into account the higher insurance premiums that owners will have to fork out.
Chua said a standard motor policy generally provided cover for risks such as accidental overturning, collision, fire, theft and impact damage due to falling objects.
He said insurers also offered EV-specific products that might cover home chargers, portable charging equipment and personal liability arising from home wall chargers.
"While EV motor insurance covers the vehicle, standard fire insurance covers property damage caused by insured perils, including fire, regardless of whether the source is an EV, petrol-powered vehicle, or other electrical source.
"However, home EV chargers are not automatically covered under standard home policies.
Permanently installed, hardwired chargers may be treated as fixtures or fittings and could fall under the building section of a home policy, depending on the policy wording."
He added that there was no general industry-wide exclusion in standard houseowner policies that automatically excluded a claim simply because a fire originated from an EV charger.
Last year, Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu told the Dewan Negara that 27 fire incidents involving electric and hybrid vehicles were reported nationwide between 2023 and July 2025.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's highway charger growth lags behind EV surge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) over the past few years has outpaced its infrastructure deployment, especially on highway charging bays, said the EV Owners Club.
Its president Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi said this has resulted in queues along major highways and there aren't enough charging bays to cater to the growing EV demand, especially during the holidays.
"Highway charging bays have only increased from 104 to 126 in the period between end-2024 and mid-2026.
The number of EVs increased from 39,000 to 122,286, in the same period.
"Personally, I have not had many issues, since I have been driving EVs for almost 10 years and have kept close tabs on where the less-crowded chargers are.
"However, many new users get caught out when travelling outside urban areas, especially along the major highways where the number of charging bays isn't nearly enough to meet demand, especially during the holidays," he told the New Straits Times.
He added that Charging Point Operators (CPOs) have been trying to address this gap.
"CPOs are constrained by high deployment costs, the need to upgrade grid connections and a fragmented and complex regulatory approval process.
"There is also the need to expand public charging networks to more rural areas, but these are low-traffic and therefore not commercially viable," he said.
He said the government can help by appointing a small Programme Management Office (PMO) to monitor EV charger deployment status as well as to identify, raise and resolve issues.
He added that it is important that this PMO be empowered to coordinate across ministries and various government departments.
[[nid:1518251]]
Meanwhile Syed Airel Haziq Danial, 21, said he plans to buy an electric vehicle (EV), but because of lack infrastructure specifically the absence of charging stations near his low-cost apartment, has prevented him from getting one.
"I intend to buy an EV because prices are affordable now.
Many in the B40 group can afford to own one.
Even in this residential area, there are people using EVs already.
"However, because there are no facilities here to support EV users, such as charging stations, and the living environment is also an issue, I feel improvements need to be made first," said Airel, who lives at the Abdullah Hukum apartments.
He added that he hopes there will be a safe, proper place where EV drivers can charge their cars.
Abdul Rahman Samah, 71, said he has seen an EV owner living in the area.
When asked if there was any suitable place near the parking area to install a charger, he suggested installing one outside the flat complex.
"Parking here is already very congested.
If they build a charging station, placing it outside the compound — but still nearby — would be fine.
Around here, there are a few charging stations, but not many.
"My main concern is that if a car is on the highway and suddenly runs low on battery, having to hunt for specific stations will be a real worry," he said.
A check by the New Straits Times at the low-cost apartment showed that the place was congested with vehicles double-parked.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cost, safety, infrastructure constraints deter rural petrol stations from EV charging rollout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The lack of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations at petrol stations, particularly in rural and outlying areas, is largely due to infrastructure, cost, space and safety constraints, the Petroleum Dealers Association of Malaysia (PDAM) said.
Its president Datuk Khairul Annuar Abdul Aziz said almost 70 per cent of petrol stations in Malaysia were owned by the brands themselves, with individual operators accounting for the rest.
He said while individual dealers could push for EV charging facilities, their ability to make such decisions was limited by oil companies' broader plans and practical considerations such as infrastructure and cost, particularly at smaller stations.
"The dealer doesn't have much of a say in this.
They can push for it, but the oil company has its own nationwide plan."
Khairul Annuar said the installation of EV chargers was also a "chicken and egg" situation, with charging operators reluctant to invest in areas where EV is low.
"EV operators don't want to invest in places where they know there's not much EV use and so it's not economical for them," he said.
He said operators had to consider the type of charging facility, including fast, normal, slow, AC and DC chargers, as well as the demographics and demand in an area.
This, he said, created a cycle in which charging infrastructure was concentrated in densely populated areas, while rural locations remained under-served.
"But what we need is to have infrastructure in places where there aren't enough people having EVs.
If the infrastructure is there, people will start to adopt EVs.
So, it's a chicken and egg situation," he said.
TOO COSTLY
Khairul Annuar said the cost of installing chargers was another major consideration, particularly for fast-charging facilities.
While AC chargers, including 7kW, 11kW and 22kW units, were cheaper, they could take several hours to charge an EV, making them less attractive to motorists seeking faster charging.
"People want fast charging, half an hour, 100 per cent.
But unfortunately, fast chargers require substantially higher investment.
That one is expensive," he said, estimating the cost at hundreds of thousands of ringgit.
[[nid:1518243]]
The cost could increase significantly depending on the existing electricity infrastructure at a petrol station.
"Sometimes Tenaga Nasional Berhad's grid is also not suitable.
To fix or install fast chargers, it has to be connected at medium voltage, 11kV, 33kV.
That one alone would cost hundreds of thousands of ringgit, including payments to TNB for designing the infrastructure, wiring works and so on," he said.
Khairul Annuar said location and the physical size of a petrol station also played an important role.
"Petrol dealers want it, but they don't want to invest themselves.
And the operators don't want to invest.
A lot of operators go to the heavily populated areas because that is where they can make their money," he said.
The challenge is particularly acute at smaller stations, where space could already be limited.
Apart from the physical space required for EV charging bays, operators also had to comply with safety requirements governing the distance between charging facilities and existing petrol pumps and underground fuel tanks.
"In other words, it's not that it cannot be done, but it's difficult.
Some cannot do it because they are simply too small.
Some are difficult," he said.
He said EV charging was also not necessarily an attractive business for petrol station operators.
"Initially, there was profit, but then it was overtaken by home installation of chargers.
Then they have to invest more in fast chargers."
Khairul Annuar suggested that greater government involvement might therefore be needed to address the infrastructure gap, particularly in underserved areas where private charging operators might not see sufficient commercial returns.
"The government might need to lead in that sense.
The infrastructure needs to come, and the initial EV station charger needs to come first, before more EVs come.
Then the other businesses can calculate their profit and loss.
Otherwise, it will be loss only, no profit," he said.
SAFETY CONCERNS
He said safety considerations were particularly important because petrol stations handled highly flammable fuel.
He said petrol stations also had to take into account petrol vapour released during refuelling.
"Our underground tank and our pump should be okay because they're underground.
But there will be vapour.
When people fill up with petrol, vapour comes out.
There is a fear that under certain circumstances, a spark could ignite it.
That's why there is a certain distance that the Fire Department will impose.
It's a requirement," he said.
Khairul Annuar also raised concerns about the availability of fire-safety equipment and trained personnel in the event of an EV fire.
[[nid:1518242]]
Khairul Annuar said the issue was not merely about installing charging equipment, but also ensuring stations had adequate safety measures and trained personnel to respond to emergencies.
Another consideration was the length of time EVs occupied charging bays.
He said petrol stations traditionally operated on a quick-turnaround model, with motorists expected to refuel and leave.
"Traditionally, operations at a petrol station are fast.
We want people to come in and out quickly.
Otherwise, people will park there, and others won't be able to fill up.
So, space is an issue.
We are afraid they will hog the parking," he said, adding that petrol stations would therefore need complementary businesses or facilities to give EV owners something to do while their vehicles are being charged.
GOVERNMENT'S ROLE
Khairul Annuar said the government's role could be particularly important in breaking the cycle in which low EV ownership discouraged investment in charging infrastructure, while inadequate charging infrastructure discouraged EV adoption.
"Who is going to go if there are not enough EVs?
Who is going to put (chargers) there if there's no infrastructure?
The infrastructure needs to come first," he said.
He said this was especially relevant for rural and outlying petrol stations, where physical limitations, electricity supply, safety requirements and low EV utilisation could make private investment difficult.
"So, it's not that they don't want to.
It's just difficult," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: The long wait for EV chargers [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ever heard of range anxiety or waiting anxiety?
Well, this is something many electric vehicle (EV) owners face when driving on our roads, especially when travelling long distances.
The cause of it?
A lack of public EV charging points nationwide.
The problem has now reached a point where EV owners are clamouring for a solution.
Statistics show there are 122,286 EVs on our roads compared with 6,916 public chargers as of July 31.
The government is targeting 30,000 public chargers by 2030.
The infrastructure comprises about 2,000 odd direct current (DC) fast chargers and about 4,000 alternating current (AC) chargers.
The number of EV charging points along the stretch of the north-south highway is 112 with a target of 350 to be installed by 2028.
Electric Vehicle Charging Industry Association president Lee Yuen How said more substations were needed at highway Rest and Recreation (R&R) areas and lay-bys to facilitate the deployment of EV chargers.
Lee, who is also managing director of EV Connection (JomCharge), said the national EV infrastructure strategy needed an urgent revisit as the number of EV vehicles being sold had outpaced charging infrastructure.
"We see more EVs on the road, faster than we can deploy EV chargers.
It is common to see long queues at all charging points during weekends and festive seasons.
It is no secret that we urgently need EV chargers, especially along the highway... this can only be done if more compact substations are built in all R&Rs and lay-bys for Charge Point Operators (CPO) to deploy EV chargers," he said.
NEED FOR STANDARD GUIDELINES
Lee said he hopes that the government standardises EV charger guidelines and submission procedures across all local councils to eliminate fragmented rules and speed up deployment.
JomCharge now has 1,948 charge points nationwide and has expanded its network of DC chargers to on-street parking areas, shopping malls and hotels.
"We started deploying DC chargers at highway R&Rs to connect Penang to Kuala Lumpur and Johor Baru.
In the early days we started putting EV chargers at shopping malls and hotels.
Currently, JomCharge has expanded its DC charging network to on-street parking areas under KL City Hall and Petaling Jaya City Council.
This is to cater for those staying in high-rises without EV charging facilities at their place," he said.
He added that the average price for AC chargers is 90 cents to RM1 per kWh, while DC chargers cost about RM1.30 to RM1.50 per kWh.
A check by the New Straits Times found that every CPO has a different rate for AC and DC chargers.
MORE CHARGES FOR HOLIDAY TRAVEL
Meanwhile, EV owners want more public charging stations, particularly outside major urban areas, to meet higher demand during school holidays, public holidays and festive seasons.
EV owner Husain Jahit said finding a charger was generally not difficult in the Klang Valley, but the limited number of charging bays at individual locations could become a problem during peak periods.
[[nid:1518238]]
"Some petrol stations have EV chargers, but they are very limited.
You may see only one or two units at a station.
The problem starts during school holidays and festive seasons.
You may have to wait for a charger," he said.
Husain said the longest he had waited to charge his Tesla was about 30 minutes, although he acknowledged that charging infrastructure along major highways had improved.
"Along the highways, especially towards the south, almost every petrol station or R&R has charging facilities now."
Husain, meanwhile, added that EV ownership remained considerably cheaper than running a petrol-powered vehicle, particularly for owners who could charge at home or at their workplace.
The media executive spent RM600 to RM700 a month on petrol but now saves more than 50 per cent on running costs, partly because he can charge for free at his wife's office.
Husain said expanding the charging network, particularly outside major urban areas, would be crucial as EV ownership continued to grow.
"The technology is there.
The charging infrastructure is improving but we need more chargers, especially outside major urban areas, and enough capacity to cope when people travel during the holidays," he said.
Another EV owner, Chua, 42, a civil engineer from Subang Jaya, said uncertainty over charger availability could make long-distance travel more stressful.
"Before I leave, I have to check where the chargers are and how much battery I have left.
With a petrol car, you don't really think about it.
During a normal day, it is fine.
But when everyone is travelling for Raya or during school holidays, you can reach an R&R and find all the chargers occupied.
Then you have to wait or drive to another station," Chua said.
Chua said more charging facilities were needed in smaller towns and rural areas.
"It's not just about having chargers in Kuala Lumpur and Petaling Jaya.
If you want more people to switch to EVs, they need to know they can travel confidently outside the Klang Valley.
Even one or two chargers at every major petrol station would make a big difference," Chua, who also drives a Tesla, said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US vows 'economic asphyxiation' of Iran with new sanctions
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding Washington's secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign.
The announcement comes almost six months into a war on Iran that has ground to a stalemate, with stalled peace talks and Tehran blocking most traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
Bessent earlier said the United States was declaring an "economic D-Day" on Iran, but his announcement named no specific countries beyond Iran and gave no timelines.
"Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," Bessent told journalists.
"We are going to hold everyone accountable, and this is economic asphyxiation of this regime."
He added that countries not joining US sanctions would "share in the isolation" of Iran, and noted that President Donald Trump was making phone calls to world leaders with requests to stop interactions with Tehran.
The Treasury Department said expanded secondary sanctions would target Iran's digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors.
It also issued new sanctions against 60 individuals, companies and vessels that allegedly aid Iran in oil revenue generation, weapons procurement and cyber operations.
The sanctions hit entities around the world, including in the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Europe.
Bessent vowed that any entity "that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system."
Iran had been dismissive of the threat of additional sanctions, and on Monday its economy minister predicted "another defeat" for Washington.
"We've been waiting for these plans for a long time, and the government is and was ready and has a two-year plan to manage these events," said Ali Madanizadeh.
Decades of sanctions
Iran has weathered decades of crushing international sanctions, and before the war it continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and to evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.
Asked on Monday if Chinese banks would be targeted by the new sanctions, Bessent said "no one is above the reach of US sanctions."
[[nid:1518226]]
Ali Vaez of the International Crisis Group said Washington was seeking to impose maximum economic pressure through various levers, but that Iran "has faced all of these before".
"While there is little doubt in Washington's ability to impose substantial pain, Tehran believes that it has a high threshold for absorbing it, as well as the potential to respond to financial pressure with military counterpressure," he said.
The US naval blockade of Iran has seen its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz fall from two million barrels a day pre-war to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler.
Speaking to reporters on Monday, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said that the pivot to applying economic pressure did not mean that military strikes were off the table.
"Economic pressure, we know, hurts them the most right now," he said. "But by no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz or around Iran."
For ordinary Iranians, the standoff is likely to bring only more economic pain after years of rampant inflation, which in December and January fuelled massive anti-government protests.
Sarah Hassanbeigi, a 32-year-old pharmacist in Tehran, said: "I don't think people can really take this much longer."
Pakistani delegation
Last week, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, considered a relative moderate, said Tehran should "bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power".
That followed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's appointment of hardliners to key security positions.
On Monday, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir, a key mediator in the conflict, visited Iran and met separately with Iran's president, chief negotiator and the head of its highest national security body.
The meetings took place after Trump spoke last week with Munir, a US source familiar with the matter told AFP earlier on Monday.
Islamabad was a leading mediator in talks that helped secure an April ceasefire that later fell apart. It is also a major trading partner of Iran, possibly opening it up to the threat of the new sanctions.
Oman's foreign minister was due in Iran on Tuesday, as Muscat and Tehran seek a deal on regulating passage through Hormuz.

Title: Johor Military Forces to make National Day parade debut
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE Johor Military Forces will take part in this year's National Day celebration in Putrajaya for the first time, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said participation of the Johor force was among the features of this year's celebration, which will be held at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31.
"They will take part together with their assets and a contingent of 100 members. This is one of the unique features this year," he said.
He was speaking during the handover ceremony for sponsorship contributions from strategic partners to participants of the "human graphics" performance here yesterday.
Fahmi said 1,500 students from 36 schools across Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur and Selangor would take part in the human graphics performance this year.
"The 1,500 students have shown tremendous enthusiasm, and this is their first time at the location."
He said another new feature this year was the placement of military and security assets at designated locations, allowing members of the public to view them up close.
He said the assets would be placed at Dataran Floria, the Millennium Monument and Dataran Aman throughout the celebration.
"In previous years, visitors would usually have to wait by the roadside to see, touch or board the assets.
"But this year, we have placed them at specific locations so visitors can see for themselves the assets belonging to the military, police and others."
Fahmi said the celebration would also feature more floats and contingents compared with previous years.
He said preparations for the celebration were more than 70 per cent complete, with several major structures, including the Royal Box, being set up.
He added that the government would also finalise health-related standard operating procedure for the celebration amid haze concerns.

Title: US plans to revoke tourism and business visas of up to 200,000 foreigners
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States, the Associated Press reported on Monday.
The report cited State Department documents obtained by AP and two US officials.
If the move materialised, it would be the largest single mass revocation of visas in US history, according to AP.
The State Department is expected to announce in the coming weeks the revocation of so-called B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought asylum or are now seeking asylum, the report added, saying the action will be coordinated with the Department of Homeland Security.
The B1 and B2 visas are issued for business and tourism travel.
The visa revocations would not necessarily result in immediate deportation, the AP report said, citing officials.
Most of those with asylum cases currently pending would be recategorised but would lose their status as business or tourism travellers, the report said.
Earlier on Monday, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau alleged on X that the American immigration system "has long been swamped by frivolous asylum claims".
The DHS referred questions to the State Department, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The State Department said earlier this month it had revoked more than 175,000 visas from foreign nationals under the Trump administration.
Trump has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown that he says is aimed at improving domestic security.
Rights groups say the crackdown has violated free speech and due process rights and created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.

Title: Anwar to deliver National Day address on Aug 30
Article:

PRIME Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will deliver the 2026 National Day Amanat Perdana address at Dataran Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur on Aug 30.
The event, organised by the National Unity Ministry, aims to convey the aspirations of the Madani government while fostering patriotism and national unity.
Festivities will begin at 5pm, featuring the Merdeka Eve Animation Concert, the World Festival of Lights, the Gema Perpaduan Malaysia Madani cultural showcase, a special musical performance and appearances by local artistes.
National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the country's well-being depended heavily on strong national cohesion.
"In a Malaysia rich in religious, cultural and linguistic diversity, as well as diverse customs and traditions, we must continue to cultivate an attitude of understanding, respect, acceptance and celebration.
"Let us continue to foster the spirit of mutual understanding, respect and acceptance of diversity, because it is through togetherness that Malaysia draws its strength to continue progressing in harmony and prosperity," he said in a statement yesterday.
The address will be broadcast live on TV1 and the RTMKlik application from 9.30pm.
Meanwhile, the 69th National Day parade, themed Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati, will take place at Dataran Putrajaya here on Aug 31, with more than 80,000 people expected to attend. — BERNAMA

Title: US state probes OpenAI over rogue AI hack
Article:
WASHINGTON: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI faces an investigation by the state of Alabama after the company revealed last month that its models went rogue and hacked an AI platform during testing.
In mid-July, two OpenAI models escaped their confined testing environment and gained access to the internet, where they found and attacked Hugging Face, a site AI developers use to store and share models and data sets.
The incident raised alarm about the dangers of AI systems acting autonomously and breaking guardrails set by human programmers to prevent safety violations.
In a 14-page order, the office of Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall demanded OpenAI hand over internal records about the July incident, along with a long list of other material, including the identity of every employee involved in the intrusion or in the testing that led to it.
It is the first known state investigation into whether an AI system attacking another company's infrastructure amounts to a violation of consumer protection law – a finding that would expose the company to major litigation across the United States.
On Aug 3, Alabama and 14 other states wrote to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman asking the company to preserve records on the incident and halt any internal cybersecurity evaluations of its models.
A spokesperson for the Alabama attorney general's office could not confirm whether OpenAI had agreed to abide by that demand.
OpenAI said in a statement to the tech news site TechCrunch that it was "conducting a thorough review along with external advisors."
"Once the review is complete, we will share a technical report with relevant government authorities and publish our findings publicly," it added.

Title: Top court upholds Trump bid to curb mail-in ballots for now
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court gave President Donald Trump a temporary victory on Monday in his bid to curb the use of mail-in ballots.
Trump signed an executive order in March seeking to restrict mail-in voting but it was immediately met with multiple legal challenges.
The three liberal justices on the Supreme Court dissented with Monday's decision that would allow parts of Trump's executive order to go ahead.

Title: Nation's leading index rises 1.3pc to 114.8 points in June
Article:

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's leading index posted an annual growth of 1.3 per cent to 114.8 points in June, reflecting the strengthening of the nation's trade activities, said the Statistics Department.
The index was driven by a surge in real imports of basic precious and non-ferrous metals (35.1 per cent), as well as real imports of semiconductors (14.2 per cent).
"This scenario is in line with the strengthening of Malaysia's trade activities, particularly sustained demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products," said the department yesterday.
However, the overall performance was partly offset by declines in several components, notably the number of new companies registered.
On a monthly basis, the index also recorded a marginal increase of 0.02 per cent, contributed mainly by real imports of other basic precious and other non-ferrous metals (0.8 per cent).
The department said the long-term smoothed trend of the leading index remained below 100 points.
"Nevertheless, the economy is expected to continue growing, supported by resilient domestic demand and continued expansion in investment activities.
"At the same time, an increasingly dynamic global economic landscape and the recovery in international trade are expected to continue supporting Malaysia's economic growth," it added.
For current economic performance, the coincident index rose 2.6 per cent year-on-year with 131.6 points, underpinned by strong growth in all components, particularly real contributions of the Employees Provident Fund (16 per cent) and the volume index of retail trade (4.1 per cent).

Title: Tornado tears through French village, dozens injured
Article:
POMAS: A tornado tore through a village in southwestern France on Monday, injuring 41 people and damaging hundreds of homes, authorities said.
French authorities had placed swathes of the country's southwest on orange alert for storms, and numerous areas were hit by power outages and transport chaos.
In the Aude department, officials cancelled the third stage of the Vuelta a Espana cycling race, which was being held in the area, when a hailstorm forced riders to seek shelter.
The tornado hit hardest in the village of Pomas, population 1,000, damaging an estimated 300 homes, in some cases ripping their roofs off.
More than 120 emergency workers were deployed to the scene, local authorities said.
Fifteen of the injured were taken to hospital.
[[nid:1518200]]
They included a pregnant woman who was hurt when her house collapsed on her, her husband told AFP.
The national weather service, Meteo-France, said winds had reached up to 117 kilometres (73 miles) per hour in the nearby village of Arquettes-en-Val.
Storms across southern France upended the transportation network, delaying trains, forcing road closures, and causing delays and cancellations at airports in Bordeaux, Marseille, Nice, Toulouse and even Paris to the north, said Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot.
An estimated 2,800 homes were left without electricity across 10 villages, officials said.
France sees several dozen tornadoes per year on average.
The impact of global warming on their frequency and intensity is unclear, according to Meteo-France.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK's Burnham says glorifying dangerous driving on social media is 'reprehensible'
Article:
LONDON:  British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday glorifying dangerous driving on social media was "truly reprehensible", as his government urged tech companies to remove videos following a car crash over the weekend that killed seven people.
A car driven the wrong way down a major road crashed into a police armed response vehicle in northeast England, killing all five occupants and two officers, in the early hours of Saturday morning.
Four of the five occupants of the car that crashed had previous convictions, police said.
Police said on Monday they had arrested 12 people in a probe into organised criminal activity linked to the incident.
The crash followed two recent head-on collisions near Dublin, one of which killed five people, which prompted Ireland's police chief to warn that some young people were driving the wrong way on the motorway "for social media likes."
Police, however, said there was currently no evidence that the events leading up to the crash had been filmed to appear on short-form video platform TikTok.
Burnham said it was a "devastating incident" and as an investigation was ongoing, there was a limit on what he could say at this time.
"But of course, anybody who glorifies dangerous driving is doing something that is truly reprehensible and unacceptable," he told reporters in Kyiv on Monday.
His spokesperson said the government had raised the issue of videos of dangerous driving with social media companies since the tragedy and made it clear that they should be removed.
Police said officers had received reports before the crash of two cars being driven dangerously, including a vehicle that was seen ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area in northeast England.
Both vehicles had been operating with cloned number plates to avoid detection, police said.
Police said inquiries over the weekend had resulted in the arrests of nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, across the Teesside area.
The suspects were arrested on suspicion of offences ranging from possession of a firearm to participating in the activities of an organised crime group, police said.
"This has been a fast-moving and complex investigation, with significant links to serious and organised criminal activity," Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said in a statement.

Title: Maharashtra food safety chief takes down unhygienic food outlets
Article:
TUKARAM    Mundhe is an Indian bureaucrat on a mission.
As Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration   commissioner, the 51-year-old has raided food businesses in the country's commercial capital Mumbai in an unprecedented crackdown on poor hygiene and unsafe food that has captivated the public nationwide.
Mundhe has led the suspension of food permits of four Domino's and one Pizza Hut outlet in recent weeks, and has also targeted cricket clubs, hotels and well-known restaurants in over 3,000 raids since he took over as Maharashtra's food safety chief in May.
When a Mumbai judge accused Mundhe of selective aggression towards private outlets and asked if court canteens were checked, his teams conducted inspections there within hours, shutting some of them which operated without licences.
"Those who try to not comply, they will face what is expected from the regulator," said Mundhe in an interview.
"You are dealing with the lives of people."
Even though foreign chains such as Domino's and McDonald's are fast expanding, it is local eateries, roadside kiosks and small restaurants — long dogged by concerns over hygiene — that remain hugely popular.
Each year since 2020, Indian food inspectors have checked over 100,000 food samples and found roughly 20 per cent to be unsafe, substandard or lacking proper labels, government data shows.
Nearly 8,000 food business licences have been cancelled in the last three years.
"Everyone has tried to normalise this for years by saying it happens in India. It's basically bottled-up anger," said Ankur Bisen, a partner at consumer consulting firm The Knowledge Company.
"I have never seen anyone like Mundhe. It's giving people hope."
Mundhe has an unconventional operating style.
He has featured in TV interviews declaring nobody dare bribe him, and that he is not afraid of administrative action despite being transferred numerous times in his 21-year career as an officer of the highly regarded Indian Administrative Service.
"I get transferred every year," he said in a 2018 interview.
Now, his food safety team's actions go viral daily — raids lead to detailed public statements and graphic images that show interiors of eateries and grocery warehouses with stained walls, crawling cockroaches and rats, and even expired food — photos that have shocked many Indians.
In Mumbai, Reuters visits last week to 25 street vendors and restaurants showed heightened fear about Mundhe's raids.
One vendor has swapped artificial red dye for natural chilli in Chinese offerings, while another has started changing his frying oil three times a day and requires staff to wear gloves and head caps.
Mumbai's omnipresent street food vada pav has not escaped Mundhe's attention. In June, he prohibited use of newspapers as packaging material — often used to wrap the delicacy.
Customers are noticing the change and consuming street food more confidently.
Supriya Wagle, 14, is happy her favourite vada pav is now being packed in cleaner butter paper, saying that is "surely a relief".
After finding lapses at some Domino's and Pizza Hut stores, Mundhe's team on Friday suspended the permit of a McDonald's outlet after finding "live pest activity (cockroaches)" and "rotting food".
The three companies did not respond to Reuters queries.
Mundhe's crackdown has included action against a Mumbai British-era cricket club, a 70-year-old ice cream parlour and a 110-year-old Parsi Dairy.
He is facing criticism from businesses that say they should be given time to adapt, with some approaching the High Court and accusing his department of high-handedness.
In one case, the judges fined his department 500,000 rupees  for continued suspension of an eatery even though it improved its compliance.
At an event in New Delhi on Friday, fans clicked quick selfies with Mundhe and jostled to shake his hand.
"I don't think I'm a celebrity. I'm just a food safety commissioner."
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump heads into midterms short on foreign policy wins
Article:
With the Iran war now at a costly standoff and crises from Ukraine to Gaza still unresolved, United States President Donald Trump's ambitious foreign policy agenda appears stuck as he heads into November's midterm elections.
The setbacks are striking for a president who returned to office last year promising to be a "peacemaker" and made resolving international conflicts a centrepiece of his second-term agenda.
Trump has grown impatient with reporters' questions and even US allies. This week, he lashed out at reporters pressing him on foreign policy issues and renewed his threat to bomb Oman, a US ally negotiating with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Labour Day, on Sept 7 this year, is traditionally when election campaigns kick into high gear, and Republicans face the prospect that unresolved conflicts abroad and their economic fallout at home could cost the party its hold on Congress.
Trump has called off talks with Teheran and announced last Wednesday a new campaign of "economic warfare" against the Islamic republic in an apparent acknowledgment that months of military attacks have not forced the concessions the US wants to see.
As inflation persists and the Iran war drives up petrol prices, Trump's approval rating has fallen to another low point with just 33 per cent of Americans in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll approving of his performance.
Other efforts to broker peace have also stalled.
Last Monday, Trump's negotiator and son-in-law Jared Kushner left empty-handed from talks to advance a Gaza peace deal. And an expected visit to Kyiv by Kushner and Trump envoy Steve Witkoff to revive long-stalled negotiations to end Russia's war in Ukraine has yet to happen.
The conflict with Iran has weighed "intensely" on the president and there is no consensus inside the White House on how to resolve it, said one Trump ally on condition of anonymity.
The pressure could increase if investors conclude the war will drag on, driving up US borrowing costs and further constraining Trump's domestic agenda.
Some experts give Trump credit for a willingness to grapple with issues they believe other presidents have been unable or unwilling to solve.
Trump has upended traditional diplomatic norms of peacemaking, relying on leveraging America's economic and military might including with US allies, but that unorthodox style has yielded mixed results.
He brought parties to the table with the aim of ending Russia's invasion of Ukraine, but the longest war in Europe since World War 2 is nowhere near ending, with the latest Russian air strikes killing 16 people in the Ukrainian capital last Thursday.
In Gaza, mediators fear that intensifying Israeli strikes on the enclave undermine efforts to end the conflict and advance a peace plan Trump forged in October last year.
In Lebanon, Israeli air strikes killed 11 people on Sunday even as a US-mediated peace framework between the two countries remains in effect.
One notable success came in Venezuela, where the US military captured President Nicolas Maduro without US casualties.
Analysts say the operation helped convince Trump that joining Israel in attacking Iran would also proceed smoothly.
But they also say that proved a miscalculation. They argue Trump has relied too heavily on applying coercive pressure even though Iran's leaders have little incentive to back down and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
"He is obsessed with applying coercion, and sometimes flattery, to bend others to his will, but oblivious to their strategic goals and domestic politics. As a result, he keeps flailing and failing," said Stephen Wertheim, a senior fellow at Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.
Meanwhile, the political clock is ticking, with Trump's Republican Party facing elections that could cost it control of one or both chambers of Congress and sharply curtail his ability to advance his agenda during his final two years in office.
Trump's reliance on coercive pressure can bring adversaries to the table but often fails to produce lasting settlements, a dynamic that may encourage rivals to wait him out.
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sweden remands school attack suspect in custody
Article:
STOCKHOLM: Swedish prosecutors said Sunday that an 18-year-old man arrested during a fatal sword attack at a high school had been remanded in custody on charges of murder and attempted murder.
The alleged attacker entered the Brinell school in the small town of Fagersta on Friday afternoon, just days after its students had returned from summer break.
Early media reports said the suspect was shot by police. Police on Saturday clarified they had shot at the suspect before detaining him, but that the suspect had not been hit.
"The 18-year-old man who was arrested on suspicion of murder and attempted murder in Fagersta on Aug 21 was remanded in custody on Sunday by the Vastmanland District Court, on probable cause suspected of the offences," the Swedish prosecution authority said in a statement.
It added that the investigation was "in an early and intensive phase."
Police on Saturday identified the one fatality in the attack as a 17-year-old girl.
Three boys were also wounded, two of them seriously.
The school was still cordoned off on Sunday, according to public broadcaster SVT.
Local police chief Tommy Alriksson told reporters on Friday that investigators were seeking a motive.
"We are looking into several leads... We are trying, of course, to remain as open-minded as possible," Alriksson said.
SVT reported that the perpetrator had a previous assault conviction and wore a helmet and carried a sword – reminiscent of a 2015 school attack in the western town of Trollhattan in which a 21-year-old killed three people in a racially motivated attack.
Media reported a TikTok account belonging to the youth was being investigated. The account has been taken down.
AFP viewed the account before it was taken down and it had several videos referencing school attacks. The last update showed a photo of a sword.
On Saturday, officers had conducted around 80 interviews and were planning to question nearly all the school's staff and students – almost 450 people – according to police chief Alriksson.
Two addresses linked to the attacker in Fagersta were also searched.

Title: Belgian pie-thrower, scourge of celebrities, dies at 80
Article:
BRUSSELS: Belgian comedian Noel Godin, who made a name throwing custard pies at celebrities from French film legend Jean-Luc Godard to tech titan Bill Gates, has died at the age of 80, his partner told AFP Monday.
Nicknamed "the Glooper" for his cries of "Gloop! Gloop!" after each strike, Godin spent more than three decades lobbing pies at rich and famous targets he felt needed bringing down a notch.
He died on Sunday morning, his partner Sylvie Broodthaers told AFP.
Describing himself as an "anarcho-confectioner," Godin began his campaign with a pie in the face of author Marguerite Duras in 1969.
His high-profile targets went on to include the future French president Nicolas Sarkozy in 1997 – although in that case he had an accomplice lob the actual pie for fear of being recognised.
Godin's pie-throwing movement hit global headlines the following year after a successful hit on Microsoft boss Gates – inspiring successors including the Taart movement in The Netherlands, the Biotic Baking Brigade in the United States or the "Entartistes" in Canada.
But he once told AFP he systematically refused contract pie attacks, even when offered "a lot of money" to target A-listers Sharon Stone and Catherine Deneuve at the Cannes Film Festival.
"We're not mercenaries," he said in a 2021 interview, describing himself as pursuing "a burlesque form of pacifism."
"An aggressive pacifism, obviously, but we only bruise our victims' egos," he said.
A 2002 hit on the French presidential candidate Jean-Pierre Chevenement – with a pineapple-flavoured missile at the Paris book fair – would lead custard-pie throwing to be ruled a criminal offence.
Convicted and fined after the Chevenement strike, Godin's case went all the way to France's top court, where he lost his final appeal – with more than 1,000 supporters throwing a raucous fundraising party to cover his legal costs.
Godin's target of choice over the years was the flamboyant French philosopher Bernard Henri-Levy, hit no fewer than eight times between 1985 and 2015, not counting copycat attacks by others around the world.
"To be honest, when he is no longer around, I'll be at a loss," Godin quipped to AFP.

Title: France readies high school phone ban for next month
Article:
PARIS: The French government said Monday it would press ahead with a ban on mobile phones in high schools from next month, but trade unions warned that the measure might be hard to implement quickly.
In July, France's parliament approved legislation banning both social media access for children under 15 and mobile phone use in high schools.
It is part of a push by President Emmanuel Macron for children to spend less time in front of screens, which the government fears is arresting their development.
But earlier this month, the country's top court struck down the social media provision, dealing a blow to Macron.
However the Constitutional Council did not rule on the separate provision banning mobile phone use in high schools.
On Monday, government spokesperson Maud Bregeon said Macron "has decided to promulgate the law" containing the ban on phones, despite the Constitutional Council striking down its flagship provision.
"As a result, the ban on mobile phones in high schools can take effect from the start of the new school year, with a stable, consolidated and statutory legal framework," she said after a cabinet meeting.
France's school year starts in September.
France has already banned children from using mobile phones in colleges – the schools attended between the ages of 11 and 15 – and in primary schools.
In early July, high schools had been instructed to prepare for the measure's implementation in September, ahead of its adoption by parliament later that month.
In order to enforce the ban, schools must amend their internal regulations.
But many schools may struggle to implement the measure because they have had little time to prepare.
Francois Resnais, national secretary of SNPDEN-Unsa, France's top union of school principals, criticised the timing as "bad."
"Schools are not ready," Resnais told AFP.
"Schools are starting the year with a rule that is not written into their internal regulations, except perhaps for those that tried to anticipate something, but that remains very limited."
[[nid:1518183]]
Christelle Kauffmann, the union's deputy secretary-general, is among the minority of school leaders who anticipated the measure.
At her high school, phones will be banned in corridors and school buildings from the start of term, but allowed outdoors.
She said it could take nearly a year before the ban could be fully implemented across all high schools.
"It is very difficult for a school community to impose a new rule on young people. Even if the law is supposed to apply automatically, it is not that simple," she said. "You cannot put a supervisor behind every student."
Kamel Chibli, vice president of the Occitanie regional council in southern France, said digital pouches and lockers used to store smartphones cost the regional authorities around 40,000 euros for a high school with 1,500 students.
High school students regularly use their smartphones to check timetable changes, room assignments and other school information.
Some teachers also rely on phones in class for research, exercises and document sharing.
In its guidance, the education ministry allows exemptions from the ban for "educational uses" or for purposes "necessary for the proper functioning of the school."
Macron's office has said the president has no plans to give up on his push to bar children from apps such as TikTok and the government would work on a new draft law.
"The president's objective is to have a stable legal framework in place by next spring to protect our children and young people," said Bregeon.
Macron is due to step down next spring after serving the maximum two consecutive terms allowed in office.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Perkeso's challenge amid evolving fraud
Article:
THE Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) deserves credit for taking an increasingly sophisticated approach to tackling fraud, particularly as criminal networks become more adept at exploiting government assistance and social protection programmes.
At the same time, the fight cannot stop at arrests. Perkeso's call for greater digital integration of medical records and stronger information-sharing among agencies is the sensible next step.
A social protection system handling billions of ringgit in contributions and payouts must continuously strengthen its safeguards.
Perkeso must, therefore, be encouraged to maintain its vigilance, invest in smarter fraud detection systems and pursue every link in the chain — while ensuring legitimate claimants are not made to bear the burden of increasingly complex controls.
The number of company executives and doctors facing court action over alleged false Perkeso claims itself highlights the growing complexity of fraud cases.
Cases may have declined, but Perkeso is seeing a worrying trend involving suspicious claims linked to government assistance programmes.
Its group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed told this newspaper that those involved were continually  adapting their methods and looking for new ways to circumvent controls.
Fraud involving employers, doctors, runners and shell companies demonstrates why enforcement must target entire networks. Some sophisticated syndicates operate  through networks beginning with doctors, employers, shell company owners, "ghost workers" and runners. For the moment, this is how Perkeso detects fraud.
Once claims trigger fraud detection filters or other red flags, they are sent to the Anti-Fraud, Ethics and Integrity Division for further investigation, a process that may well take several weeks to eight months.
Perkeso is rightly calling for  greater digital integration in the healthcare system. Such an integrated system will allow authorised hospitals and clinics to submit medical reports and other relevant records directly to Perkeso, reducing the agency's need to rely on documents submitted by claimants or intermediaries. More of this must happen to ensure more effective verification.
A direct link between the healthcare system and Perkeso would certainly minimise opportunities for document manipulation, strengthen fraud detection and protect the integrity of the social security system.
Syndicates have found a new way to "earn" income. We must not allow them to destroy a social security system that has been built and improved over the years. Retrospective reviews of approved claims show that enforcement does not end once money has been paid.
The RM61 million in prevented wrongful payouts and RM3.8 million recovered demonstrate the value of sustained enforcement. Stronger penalties should target facilitators and organisers, not merely those who submit fraudulent claims.
The challenge is to strengthen safeguards without creating unnecessary hurdles for genuine beneficiaries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Southern Thailand hit by fresh attack after 51 incidents
Article:
KOTA BARU: Barely 48 hours after 51 locations across three provinces in southern Thailand were hit by a series of attacks, another similar incident occurred tonight.
The latest incident occurred in Mayo district, Pattani, where a 7-Eleven convenience store in Village 3, Langa subdistrict, was attacked about 8pm (Thai time).
A Thai security spokesman said several assailants entered the store and ordered employees to leave before an explosion occurred.
"Gunfire was also reported during the incident.
"Thai authorities were immediately deployed to the scene, while security personnel secured the area and began assessing the situation," he said.
The spokesman said further details, including whether there were any casualties or damage, had yet to be confirmed.
The incident came after coordinated attacks hit
51 locations
across Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala on Saturday night, raising concerns over renewed violence in Thailand's southern border provinces.
The attacks, including those involving improvised explosive devices (IEDs), left two Thai nationals injured.

Title: Museum heists more violent, with thieves hired on social media, Europol says
Article:
BRUSSELS: Art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies focusing on gold and jewels, and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad-hoc opportunists recruited through social media, Europol said on Monday.
The heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris in October last year was a prime example of these shifts, Europol said, as the thieves threatened guards and visitors, and stole €88 million worth of jewels such as Empress Eugenie's tiara.
Over the last two years, art thieves have shifted their attention to precious metals, jewels and cultural artefacts that offer greater profits, the EU's law enforcement agency said in a report.
The price of gold has surged 85 per cent over the past two years, as investors and central banks turn to the metal as a safe haven.
The London Bullion Market Association, which oversees London's over-the-counter gold trading hub, has warned that "as gold prices rise to historic levels, illicit flows and market distortions are also increasing."
Europol said: "offenders are breaching premises and display cases using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars and, in some instances, explosives."
Where traditional gangs used "deception and stealth", had a central leader and niche expertise, recent thefts were carried out by a decentralised ad-hoc group of profit-seeking opportunists, recruited through social media on a "crime-as-a-service" basis, it said.
Europol added thieves were increasingly targeting gold items from nuggets and coins to jewels.
"Precious metals can be easily melted down, leaving no trace for law enforcement, and facilitating illicit sales during the fencing process.
Precious stones in jewellery, on the other hand, can be easily removed and sold further," the report said.
In January last year, thieves used explosives to steal a 2,500-year-old Dacian golden helmet and three ancient gold bracelets from a museum in the Netherlands.
The artefacts were later recovered and returned to Romania, although one bracelet is still missing.
Europol also noted an increase in thefts of ancient Chinese porcelain artefacts such as Ming Dynasty vases due to high demand.

Title: Anwar calls for stronger government delivery, communication
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the government to continuously strengthen its delivery and communication.
In a Facebook post, Anwar, who is also finance minister, said this was crucial to ensure that every policy, initiative and reform implemented by the government was understood and its benefits felt by the people.
"This was among the matters emphasised while chairing a special meeting of the prime minister with ministry secretaries-general and heads of service this afternoon.
"This periodic meeting aims to examine the strengthening of governance and the implementation of reforms within the government administration," he said.
Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar was also present at the meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Geng Manap' busted over motorcycle thefts, house break-in
Article:
IPOH: Police have busted a criminal gang known as Geng Manap believed to be involved in a series of motorcycle thefts and a house break-in in the district.
Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said six suspects, aged between 27 and 66, were arrested in several operations carried out between Aug 11 and 18.
"A total of 20 motorcycle frames and eight sacks containing motorcycle components were seized.
"Investigations revealed that the group was linked to 14 motorcycle theft cases and one house break-in," he said in a statement tonight.
He said the cases were investigated under Sections 411, 414, 457 and 374A of the Penal Code and Section 29(1) of the Minor Offences Act 1955.
Some of the suspects were charged in court today, while others were released on bail of between RM3,000 and RM5,000 pending case mention, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police seek public help to locate missing KAFA teacher
Article:
BALIK PULAU: Police are seeking public assistance to locate a 26-year-old Kafa teacher who has been missing since leaving his home in Sungai Ara on Aug 22.
Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said police received a report from the man's father on Aug 23.
"The missing man, Mohamad Hijazi Zamri, is believed to have sought his mother's permission to go to Surau Al-Muttaqin in Lilitan Sungai Ara on a blue Yamaha LC135 motorcycle bearing registration number PQG 275.
"However, he did not return home and could not be contacted by his family," he said tonight.
Anuwal said Hijazi was 155cm tall and weighed 54kg, with a medium-tan complexion and short black hair.
He was last seen wearing an orange and black long-sleeved T-shirt and black trousers.
"We urge anyone with information on his whereabouts to contact the Southwest District Police Headquarters at 04-866 2222 or any nearby police station to assist investigations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Nancy seeks additional RM168mil for welfare
Article:
KUCHING: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry has proposed an additional RM168 million under the 2027 Budget to strengthen welfare support for target groups, including the care sector.
Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the proposal included additional support for caregivers of the elderly, many of whom provided unpaid care at home.
"The ministry has proposed a total welfare allocation of nearly RM4 billion, including about RM3 billion for existing welfare recipients, while the additional allocation includes measures to strengthen the care sector," she told a press conference after launching the Care Sector Initiative under the Madani 2026 Budget here today.
Meanwhile, Nancy said the government aimed to produce 50,000 caregivers for the elderly, persons with disabilities (PwD), children and the community, as well as welfare officers.
"This year, we are targeting 2,000 caregivers by April," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid, Fadillah urge Muslims to embody Prophet's values
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maulidur Rasul should be observed by commemorating the birth of Prophet Muhammad and emulating his sirah, character and Sunnah as guidance in all aspects of life, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
In a Facebook post, he expressed hope that Maulidur Rasul 1448H would continue to nurture Muslims' love for the Prophet, strengthen brotherhood and inspire them to contribute to society.
"May this celebration continue to foster our love for the Prophet, strengthen our bonds of brotherhood and inspire us to become a community that brings mercy and goodness to society at large, Insya-Allah," he said.
Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said Maulidur Rasul was not merely about recalling the Prophet's life or reciting selawat, but about embodying his Sunnah and character in daily life.
He said Prophet Muhammad was the qudwah and uswatun hasanah, or best role model, in demonstrating compassion, trustworthiness, justice, patience and ihsan.
"The Prophet also demonstrated how differences can be managed with wisdom, how brotherhood can be preserved, and how a society can be built upon mutual respect and harmonious living," he said.
Fadillah urged Muslims not to allow differences to become sources of division, but to choose compassion over hostility, wisdom over emotion, brotherhood over discord and noble character over conflict.
He said these values aligned with this year's Maulidur Rasul theme, "Madani Dihayati, Ummah Diberkati", which calls on Muslims to translate trustworthiness, benevolence, courtesy and mutual respect into daily life while strengthening unity.
Fadillah also urged Muslims to emulate the Prophet in their work, family life, community interactions and civic responsibilities.
"May Malaysia continue to be safeguarded by Allah with peace, unity and harmony, and may all its people be blessed with a prosperous and blessed life," he said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police chase uncovers 442kg of cooking oil in MPV
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A police chase involving a suspicious vehicle in Chalok, Setiu, led to the discovery of 442kg of 1kg packets of cooking oil in a Nissan Grand Livina.
Terengganu Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director Mohd Mufsi Lat said the Hulu Terengganu KPDN branch received the case from the police following the discovery.
He said the incident began when police spotted a suspicious vehicle and gave chase before it crashed.
"An inspection was carried out after the vehicle crashed, leading to the discovery of cooking oil inside, along with a local male driver in his 50s.
"Following the handover of the case, the Hulu Terengganu KPDN branch opened an investigation paper under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 for further action," he said.
The man was also detained to assist investigations.
Following the discovery, KPDN seized the Nissan Grand Livina and its keys, as well as 442kg of 1kg packets of cooking oil found inside the vehicle.
Mufsi said the total value of the seizure was estimated at RM21,105.
He said investigations would continue to determine the source, ownership and purpose of the cooking oil, as well as whether any provisions of the law had been breached.
He said KPDN would continue to step up enforcement efforts to curb the diversion and misuse of controlled goods that could affect consumers' interests.
"Members of the public with information on any activities involving the diversion or misuse of controlled goods can channel complaints to KPDN through its official channels.
"KPDN also appreciates the cooperation and swift action by the police in assisting with enforcement action in this case," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five main Kajang roads to close from Wednesday for Merdeka eve
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five main roads around Kajang will be closed in stages from Wednesday and fully closed on Aug 30 for the 2026 Selangor State Merdeka Eve Celebration at Kajang Stadium.
Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the closures were aimed at ensuring smooth traffic flow and public safety during the celebration.
He said Jalan Mahkamah would be fully closed from Aug 26 to 30, while Jalan Cempaka Putih, Jalan Cempaka Kuning, Jalan Stadium and Jalan Cheras would be closed in stages.
"The staged closures for rehearsals will be from 8.30am to 10.30am and 7pm to 10pm on Aug 28, and from 7pm to 10pm on Aug 29.
"All roads involved will then be fully closed on Aug 30 from 8am until the event ends," he said in a statement today.
Naazron advised the public to plan their journeys and use alternative routes to avoid congestion around the venue.
Motorists are also urged to comply with instructions from police personnel deployed at the scene.
Organisers have provided designated parking areas around the venue, while shuttle bus services will operate from several major rail stations, including Sungai Jernih and Bukit Dukung MRT stations, Jalan Bukit MRT station, Jalan Reko LRT station and Kajang 2 LRT station.
Naazron said medical personnel and ambulances from Kajang Hospital, St John Ambulance, Kajang Plaza Medical Centre (KPMC) and the Malaysian Armed Forces would also be stationed at strategic locations.
Members of the public with traffic-related enquiries or complaints can contact the district police headquarters control centre at 03-8911 4222.
